nurture.subject: Your Courier Startup Checklist is here

nurture.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

One thing that separates couriers who stick with it from those who burn out early: knowing your lanes.

A lane is simply the corridor you run — for example, Milwaukee to Chicago, or local metro pickups. Knowing your preferred lanes before you start helps you:

  • Talk clearly with brokers about what you can and can't cover
  • Plan your days so you're not crisscrossing the city unpaid
  • Decide which loads fit your schedule and equipment

Practical step: write down your 2–3 preferred lanes and the hours you can run them. Keep it somewhere you'll see it before you accept work.

Tomorrow I'll share the other half of the equation — what the back office of a courier business actually looks like, and why it's the part that sinks most new operators.

— TransitNow, {{business_phone}}
nurture.subject: The one thing to figure out before your first route

nurture.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Most new couriers are good at the driving part. The part that gets them is everything else:

  • Researching loads and figuring out which are real
  • Vetting brokers and carriers before committing
  • Chasing rate confirmations and keeping paperwork straight
  • Coordinating pickup and delivery times
  • Planning routes so the day actually works

That's the back office of a one-truck business — and it's a second job.

Some operators handle it all themselves. Others use dispatch support to stay organized while they focus on the road. Neither is wrong; it depends on how you work and what your time is worth.

If you want to see how we handle it for our clients, {{product_name}} covers lane research, load-search prep, broker verification guidance, scheduling coordination, paperwork guidance, and route planning — a monthly subscription, cancel anytime. See the details

No guaranteed work, no guaranteed income — just organized support for an independent operation.

postPurchase.subject: How to get maximum value from your subscription

postPurchase.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Quick tip this week: build a paperwork habit.

Every load generates documents — rate confirmations, bills of lading, delivery receipts, invoices. The operators who stay organized photograph or file each document the same day it arrives.

A simple system that works:

  • One folder per week (or per load)
  • Photo of every signed document before you leave the dock
  • Rate confirmation saved before you start the run

It takes five minutes a day and saves hours at tax time — or when a payment dispute comes up.

Need help organizing yours? That's part of what your subscription covers. Just ask.

— The TransitNow team

roomWelcome.subject: Your first assignment: name your one thing
roomWelcome.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Name your ONE thing. Write one sentence that finishes this: "90 days from now, I want ___ in motion." One idea, one skill, one stream of income — not five. The members who get the most out of the Room are the ones who pick one thing and give it 90 days.

Davena Juanette Blue

roomWelcome.subject: How the Room actually works
roomWelcome.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Quick orientation so you get the full value of your membership:

1. The classroom. Work it in order: 00 Start Here, then 01 through 04. Each module is wealth-building education plus practical action steps — not theory to collect, but moves to make.

2. Your 90-day goal. One goal, twelve weeks. Everything in the Room points back to it.

3. Weekly check-ins. Every week you report what you did and what's next. Twelve check-ins, one per week — this is the accountability engine.

4. Daily nudges. A short accountability message every day to keep your goal in front of you.

5. The community. People building alongside you. Ask questions, share wins, learn from others doing the work.

Education, action, accountability — that's the whole system. CONTINUE IN THE ROOM

Davena Juanette Blue
Wealth Builder's Room

  2. What are your 3 smallest actions for next week?

Log in and submit it — this is the rhythm that makes the Room work: one check-in per week, twelve weeks, one goal getting closer every time.

SUBMIT YOUR WEEK 1 CHECK-IN

Small completions, every week. That's how wealth gets built.
Davena Juanette Blue
Wealth Builder's Room

roomWelcome.subject: Two weeks in — the only rule that matters
roomWelcome.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Two weeks into the Room. Here's the only rule that matters from here on:

Don't start over. When a shiny new idea shows up — and it will — write it down and keep working your one thing. Finishing one thing teaches you more about building than starting ten things.

Your ideas can become income. Your income can become wealth. But only the ideas you finish.

Hit reply and tell me: what's your one thing? A real person reads every response.

BACK TO THE ROOM

Keep going.
Davena Juanette Blue
Wealth Builder's Room

roomNurture.subject: Your ideas need a plan
roomNurture.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Here's a simple practice that changes how wealth gets built: capture every idea in one place. One notebook, one note on your phone, one list — not ideas scattered across sticky notes, screenshots, and half-remembered thoughts.

Once a week, look at that list and ask: which ONE of these is worth 90 days of my attention? Ideas you don't review are just entertainment. Ideas you review become options.

roomNurture.subject: Stop starting over
roomNurture.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Most people don't fail at building wealth because their ideas are bad. They fail because they start over — a new idea every month, a new plan every quarter, nothing finished.

Try the one-project rule: pick one thing and give it 90 days of real effort before you allow yourself to chase the next shiny idea. Write the start date down. Finishing one thing teaches you more about building than starting ten things.

That's the spirit of the Wealth Builder's Room — one 90-day plan at a time, with education, action steps, and a community learning alongside you. Join the Wealth Builder's Room — $49/month

roomNurture.bodyHtml:

Write down one sentence that finishes this: "90 days from now, I want ___ in motion." Then write what "done" looks like, in concrete terms. Vague goals get vague effort; a defined target tells you what to do on Monday morning.

roomNurture.subject: The 90-day shift
roomNurture.bodyHtml:
Hi {{first_name}},

Ninety days feels long and short at the same time — long enough to build something real, short enough to stay focused. The trick: don't plan the 90 days. Plan the next seven.

Take your one goal and ask: what are the 3 smallest actions I can do this week? Do them. Next week, pick 3 more. Twelve weeks of small, finished actions beats one giant plan you never start. Momentum is a side effect of small completions.

The Wealth Builder's Room is built around exactly this rhythm — the 90-Day Wealth Action Plan, broken into steps, with a community keeping each other honest. Join the Wealth Builder's Room — $49/month
